text:
Alex (customer): Hey team — since last night ~00:30 UTC a bunch of our API calls are hitting us-east even though our tenant is pinned to eu-west. Latency triples and some requests 403 (auth) from the model service. Billing spike. Can you check routing/failover for tenant `acme-inc`?

Maya (support): Sorry about that Alex — looking now. Can you paste an example request id or header? Also, do you see any cookies/affinity headers on your client?

Alex (customer): request_id=req_0a1b2c3d , header x-redwood-region: eu-west, but response shows x-serving-region: us-east. No explicit cookie from our side.

Maya (support): Thx. Looping in SRE. @Leo any immediate visibility?

Leo (SRE): I can see a surge of traffic routed to us-east for that tenant. Checking failover policy for the tenant now. Pulling config: `redwoodctl tenants get acme-inc --failover`

routing-bot: Retrieved failover policy v2 for tenant acme-inc (id: ff12). Priority order: ["us-east","eu-west"], sticky: true, weights: {"us-east": 60, "eu-west": 40}.

Leo (SRE): ok — that priority array is inverted. The tenant UI shows eu-west first but the stored policy has us-east first. That matches why requests are preferring us-east as primary. Looks like a config merge/serialization bug flipped the list order during a recent rollout.

Jordan (eng-runtime): Oof. We had a migration that normalized arrays -> dedup -> sort for stable hashing, but we forgot that priority arrays are order-sensitive. I found the PR that added sort(). Will revert.

Maya (support): Alex — that explains the region mismatch. For immediate mitigation: we can set a routing override to force eu-west for your tenant while we fix the migration. Do you want us to do that?

Alex (customer): Yes please. We need low latency for customer-facing flows. Also any guidance on auth 403s?

Leo (SRE): 403s are likely from session affinity (sticky) still pointing clients to old us-east node where token cache isn't warmed or keys differ. Two-step mitigation: (1) set routing override to eu-west, (2) disable sticky for the tenant briefly to flush affinity cookies so clients reattach to eu-west.

Jordan (eng-runtime): Proposed short-term commands (on prod control plane):

```bash
# force eu-west for tenant
redwoodctl routing override set --tenant acme-inc --region eu-west --reason "emergency: inverted priority"
# disable sticky so affinity TTL clears
redwoodctl tenants update acme-inc --failover '{"priority":["eu-west","us-east"],"sticky":false}'
```

Leo (SRE): After that, watch `edges.routing.hits{tenant:acme-inc}` and `latency.p50{region}`. I can push the override now if you authorize, Alex.

Alex (customer): Authorize. Do it.

Maya (support): Doing override + disabling sticky now.

routing-bot: Applied routing override -> eu-west for tenant acme-inc at 1829500062 by Maya (support). Updated failover sticky=false (v2->v3) at 1829500075.

Leo (SRE): Metrics show route shift starting +8s after override, p50 latency back to baseline in ~40s. No more 403s in recent 5m.

Alex (customer): Confirmed — latency back to normal and 403s gone. Thanks!

Jordan (eng-runtime): Root cause: a normalization step in a config migration accidentally sorted failover.priority arrays. Action items: (1) revert sorting in migration code and add targeted unit test ensuring order preserved, (2) add a validation rule on control plane rejecting sorted priority arrays (order must match what console shows), (3) add an alert for sudden cross-region shift >50% for a tenant. I'll open PRs and a rollback plan.

Maya (support): Logged escalation ticket SUP-2026-321 and informed account team. Alex, we'll keep monitoring for 24h and follow up with postmortem + config diff.

Alex (customer): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please send the postmortem and confirm if any billing credits are available for the spike.

Maya (support): Will coordinate billing review and include in the postmortem. Closing the immediate incident but will keep the thread open for follow-up. :thumbsup:
